He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]] and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. He was an [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA national champion]] and earned [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] honors with Michigan in 2026. Johnson represented the [[United States men's national under-18 basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[2024 FIBA Under-18 AmeriCup]] and the [[2025 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2025 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]], winning a [[gold medal]] in each tournament. ==High school career== Johnson played his first three seasons at [[St. Rita of Cascia High School]] in [[Chicago]], before transferring to [[Thornton Township High School]] in [[Harvey, Illinois]] for his final season.{{cite web|url=https://www.thetelegraph.com/sports/article/morez-johnson-facts-illinois-basketball-20172140.php|title=Morez Johnson Jr.: 3 things to know about the Illinois Fighting Illini basketball forward|website=The Telegraph |last1=Hall |first1=Erik }} As a sophomore, he was a [[Associated Press]] Class 4A second-team All-State selectee.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/entertainment-sports-basketball-illinois-high-school-basketball-aabe1472e149d2c0f504965b64869c70|title=Illinois Boys All-State Basketball Teams|accessdate=December 18, 2025|date=March 9, 2022|publisher=[[Associated Press]]}} As a junior, he was an AP Class 4A First-Team All-State selectee along with [[Jeremy Fears Jr.]], [[Owen Freeman]], [[Dai Dai Ames]] and [[Cam Christie]].{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/illinois-allstate-boys-basketball-teams-16a3972e5940f41faf17810dbc9c21e9|title=Illinois AP names All-State boys’ basketball teams|accessdate=December 18, 2025|date=March 9, 2023|publisher=[[Associated Press]]}} As a senior, he was named the [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] in 2024.{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/illinois-mr-basketball-johnson-harvey-thornton |title=Illinois Recruit Morez Johnson Wins Illinois Mr. Basketball |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=12 April 2024 }} ===Recruiting=== In April 2021, Johnson received his first division 1 offer from [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] following his freshman season. After receiving an offer from [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] in June 2021, he committed to play for his home-state school before the start of his sophomore season on November 5, 2021. At the time of his commitment he also held offers from [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], amongst others. He was ranked as the No. 1 player in the state of Illinois and the No. 30 overall player in the country in [[247Sports]] composite rankings in 2024.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/player/morez-johnson-jr-46115307/high-school-298020/ |title=Morez Johnson Jr. Recruiting Profile|website=[[247Sports]]|access-date=April 2, 2025}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|collapse=no|year=2024}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Morez Johnson Jr. | position = F/C | hometown = [[Riverdale, IL]] | highschool = Thornton Township | feet = 6 | inches = 9 | weight = 225 | 40 = | commitdate = 11/5/21 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn grade = 89 | espn stars = 4 | grayshirt = }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = | rivals ref title = | scout ref title = | espn ref title = | rivals school = | 247 school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | scout overall = | rivals overall = 27 | espn overall = 29 | 247 overall = 31 | accessdate = April 2, 2025 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===Illinois=== Johnson enrolled at the [[University of Illinois]] in 2024, playing for head coach [[Brad Underwood]] and the [[2024–25 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Fighting Illini]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thechampaignroom.com/2023/11/9/23953420/illinois-mens-womens-basketball-fighting-illini-brad-underwood-shauna-green-morez-johnson |title=Top-100 prospect Morez Johnson signs with Illinois |website=[[SB Nation]]|date=9 November 2023 }} On November 4, 2024, in his first collegiate game he had three points, eight rebounds and blocked a career-high six shots against [[2024–25 Eastern Illinois Panthers men's basketball team|Eastern Illinois]]. On November 26 against [[2024–25 Maryland Eastern Shore Hawks men's basketball team|UMES]], Johnson had 10 points and 13 rebounds in 14 minutes off the bench, his first career double-double. On January 8, 2025, he scored a career-high 20 points with 11 rebounds against [[2024–25 Penn State Nittany Lions basketball team|Penn State]], his second double-double. On February 2 against [[2024–25 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]], Johnson scored 14 points with a career-high 15 rebounds, his third double-double.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/4873153/morez-johnson-jr |title=Morez Johnson Jr. Game Log (2024-25) |website=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=April 2, 2025}} On February 15, Johnson broke his wrist against [[2024–25 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/43891363/illinois-loses-forward-morez-johnson-jr-broken-wrist |title=Illinois loses forward Morez Johnson Jr. to broken wrist |website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=17 February 2025 }} He missed the rest of the regular season and returned in the [[2025 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|2025 Big Ten tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wcia.com/sports/illini-basketball/morez-johnson-jr-to-return-for-postseason-play/|title=Morez Johnson Jr. to return for postseason play|website=WCIA.com|date=11 March 2025 }} Following the end of his freshman season, Johnson entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]]. He played in 30 games and started eight times for Illinois, averaging 7.0 points, 6.7 rebounds and 1.1 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.on3.com/news/morez-johnson-illinois-forward-plans-enter-ncaa-transfer-portal/|title=Illinois forward Morez Johnson enters NCAA transfer portal|website=[[On3.com]]|date=28 March Wolverines]] against [[2025–26 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]], he led the team in scoring with a career-high 24 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/11/03/michigan-wolverines-basketball-oakland-golden-grizzlies-season-opener/87076278007/ |title=Michigan [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] second team selection by the media and third team selection by the coaches.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/3/10/mens-basketball-lendeborg-earns-big-ten-player-of-the-year-as-u-m-hauls-15-all-conference-honors|title=Lendeborg Earns Big Ten Player of the Year as U-M points and 10 rebounds, while shooting 8-of-8 from the field. He became only the fifth player in NCAA tournament history to shoot 100% and record at least 20 points and 10 rebounds.{{cite |website=[[ESPN.com]] |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |date=April 6, 2026 |access-date=April 7, 2026}} Johnson was named to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Final Four all–tournament All-Tournament Teams|accessdate=April 13, 2026|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]}} On April 24, he declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]] after his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=https://wolverineswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/wolverines/mens-basketball/2026/04/24/morez-johnson-jr-declares-for-nba-draft/89776717007/|title=Morez Johnson Jr. declares for NBA draft but could return|author=Hole, Isaiah|date=April 24, 2026|publisher=[[USA Today]]}} ==Team USA career== Johnson represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[2024 FIBA Under-18 AmeriCup]] in Argentina. He played all six games and averaged 8.0 points, 9.0 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game, leading the United States in rebounding as they won the gold medal. Michigan Wolverines teammate [[Trey McKenney]] was also on the national team.{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/256-fiba-u18-americup/208738/stats |title=FIBA U18 AmeriCup 2024 (stats) |website=[[FIBA]] |date=June 3–9, 2024 |access-date=April 2, 2025}} The following year, Johnson was again selected for the United States national team at the [[2025 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2025 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Switzerland.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/6/20/mens-basketball-johnson-jr-named-to-team-usa-u19-squad-to-head-to-fiba-world-cup |title=Johnson Jr. Named to Team USA U19 Squad, to Head to FIBA World Cup |website=[[University of Michigan]] |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=June 20, 2025 |access-date=June 20, 2025}} He started six of the seven games, and again won a gold medal with the undefeated Team USA. In the championship game against Germany, Johnson scored 15 points and 10 rebounds. In total, he averaged 9.4 points, 6.4 rebounds and 1.7 blocks in 18.6 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2025/07/06/michigan-basketballs-morez-johnson-jr-wins-gold-with-team-usa-at-fiba-u-19-world-cup/84485944007/
